post.caption: Swatch's satellite was thrown by hand. In 1998 Swatch launched Internet Time, cutting the day into 1,000 equal beats of 86.4 seconds, starting at midnight in Biel, Switzerland. In 1999 it backed a small satellite for Russia's Mir space station, meant to broadcast Swatch ads over amateur radio. Radio hobbyists around the world protested, because those frequencies are meant to be free of advertising. Its transmitter was switched off before launch. On 16 April 1999 a French astronaut released it by hand on a spacewalk. Swatch still tells time in beats.
